assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Kiyotaki-Moore credit-cycles model shows how collateral constraints and asset prices amplify and propagate shocks. It became a foundation of modern macro-finance and of work on financial crises and policy. Its influence on both theory and practice is very large.
assessment.attribution: The core contribution is the Kiyotaki-Moore (1997) framework, which is clearly attributable to the two proposed laureates. Gertler and Gilchrist belong mainly to the related financial-accelerator line, which is already partly recognised by the 2022 prize. I therefore keep the proposal to the two originators.
assessment.maturity: Work from about 1997 has had nearly three decades of confirmation, extension and use after the 2008 crisis. It is fully mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the financial-accelerator work recognised in 2022 may make the Committee see the topic as partly covered.
The boundary between the Kiyotaki-Moore and Bernanke-Gertler-Gilchrist contributions is judged from my own knowledge and not independently checked.
Whether a third laureate should be included depends on how broadly the Committee defines the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Law and finance created a large empirical research programme linking legal origins and investor protection to financial development, ownership structure and growth. It changed how economists treat institutions in finance, corporate governance and comparative development. The legal-origins hypothesis and the measurement of the 'anti-director rights' index have both been contested.
assessment.attribution: The Law and Finance papers are jointly authored by La Porta, Lopez-de-Silanes, Shleifer and Vishny. Shleifer is the central intellectual figure and has also contributed widely beyond this topic. I propose the three most identified with the legal-origins programme. Leaving out Vishny is a real attribution risk.
assessment.maturity: The central papers date from 1997-1998, and the literature has had long scrutiny, replication and critique. The core is mature, although part of its empirical basis is disputed.
uncertainties: Critiques of the coding, causal interpretation and robustness of legal-origins results could weaken the case.
Choosing between Vishny and a three-person cap involves a difficult attribution judgement.
Institutional questions about the laureates' careers are outside the supplied evidence and are not weighed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This work changed understanding of labour demand through skill-biased and task-based technological change and through trade shocks, notably import competition from China. It offers credible empirical evidence on wage inequality, job polarisation and regional adjustment. Its relevance to automation and globalisation policy is very large.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Katz and Hanson are the most plausible three. Katz is linked to the earlier skill-premium work, Autor to the task framework and the China shock, and Hanson to the trade-shock and regional-adjustment work. Dorn is a key co-author of the China-shock papers and is left out because of the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The literature runs from the 1990s to the 2010s and has been extended and replicated widely. Some debate continues over magnitudes and over the task-based interpretation.
uncertainties: Debate continues over the long-run size and interpretation of the China-shock effects.
The three-laureate limit leaves out a major co-author, Dorn.
The task-based framework may be viewed as an accumulation of many contributors, including Acemoglu.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The New Keynesian framework with nominal rigidities, together with the associated theory of monetary policy rules, is central to modern macro and central-bank practice. The importance is very high.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across many people, including Calvo on staggered pricing, Taylor on policy rules, Woodford and Gali on the canonical framework, Christiano-Eichenbaum-Evans on estimation, Smets on estimated DSGE models and Gertler. Any three-person selection leaves important contributors out. Taylor, Woodford and Gali are the most defensible combination for rules, theory and the canonical model.
assessment.maturity: The literature is mature and long confirmed in practice, though the 2008 crisis and the post-2020 inflation raised questions about parts of the framework.
uncertainties: Attribution is very diffuse, and the three-laureate cap is a serious constraint.
Calvo, Christiano, Eichenbaum and Gertler have strong claims.
Recent inflation episodes and heterogeneous-agent critiques may lower the perceived standing of the representative-agent version.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Mian and Sufi show with micro-level data that household leverage and credit supply drive housing booms, consumption collapses and the depth of recessions. The work changed how economists understand the 2008 crisis and how they study credit cycles in macro-finance. Its empirical credibility and policy relevance are high.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are the clear originators of the household-debt programme and have worked together closely. Campbell is a major figure in household finance but is not central to this particular line.
assessment.maturity: The key papers date from 2009-2014, and the book House of Debt followed. The core findings have been widely replicated, but the work is younger than that of many candidates, and the causal interpretation of some results remains discussed.
uncertainties: The work is somewhat recent compared with a typical laureate record.
Some measurement and identification choices have been challenged, and competing explanations for the housing boom exist.
Whether the Committee prefers to wait for further consolidation is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Melitz model introduced firm heterogeneity into trade theory, with selection of exporters and reallocation across firms. It explains why gains from trade come through productivity changes within industries. It transformed both the theory and the empirics of international trade and is widely used in quantitative work.
assessment.attribution: Melitz (2003) is the foundational paper. Helpman has a strong separate claim from the earlier increasing-returns trade theory and from the heterogeneous-firm extensions with Melitz and Yeaple. Redding is a major contributor to the quantitative implementations, but his role is less foundational.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty years of work have extended and tested the framework. The empirical regularities on exporter selection are confirmed, but some welfare conclusions depend on model structure.
uncertainties: Krugman received the prize in 2008 for related trade theory, so the Committee may treat the area as partly covered.
Bernard, Eaton and Kortum have related claims that are not on this ballot entry.
Welfare implications depend on the functional forms assumed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The programme provided long-run, tax-record-based measurement of top incomes and wealth, reviving distributional questions in economics and public debate. The data contribution is substantial and the influence on research and policy is very high. Some theoretical claims, especially about r>g, are more contested than the measurement work.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are the principal pioneers of the top-income series, and Zucman extended the work to wealth and offshore holdings. Atkinson, now deceased, was a major earlier contributor. Attribution is reasonably clear for the three proposed laureates.
assessment.maturity: The top-income work dates from about 2003 and the wealth work from the 2010s. The measurement contribution is maturing, but methodological critiques of the wealth series and of the capital-share claims continue.
uncertainties: Methodological disputes over the measurement of wealth and income are not yet settled, and the policy engagement has produced disagreement within the profession.
The conceptual contribution may be judged as less central than the data contribution.
Saez also appears in the empirical optimal taxation entry, so the Committee may consider how to treat that overlap.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The weak-instruments literature changed how researchers use instrumental variables, with diagnostics and identification-robust inference widely used in applied work. The influence on practice is very large for a methods contribution. Econometrics prizes often require a very broad impact beyond one technical problem.
assessment.attribution: Staiger and Stock established the weak-instruments problem and the first-stage diagnostics. Andrews, together with Stock and Moreira, is central to robust inference procedures. Moreira and Yogo are important contributors who are left out by the three-person limit.
assessment.maturity: The central papers are from the 1990s to the 2000s and are standard in practice and textbooks, so the work is mature.
uncertainties: The contribution may be viewed as narrower than recent econometrics prizes.
Stock has related work in dynamic factor models and Andrews appears in other entries, so the Committee may see overlapping credit.
Attribution is distributed across several econometricians.
